packs.title: Art, Gardens and Bay
packs.promise: Explore art, habitat and history across separate St. Petersburg outings.

q.t: A Building for an Unusual View
q.s: Compare a museum form with the art it holds.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or official-source route.
Choose a public exterior view or an admitted gallery and notice one curve, angle or frame.
Sketch that feature and explain how it directs attention without copying an artwork.

q.s: Choose one documented habitat and an open route.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or official-source route.
Use the preserve’s current map to select an open trail segment or public boardwalk.
Record one habitat boundary and a safe return point without promising a wildlife sighting.

q.t: Where a Park Meets the Bay
q.s: Read a public shore and its protected history.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or official-source route.
From an open park path or the city’s digital archaeology tour, identify a shoreline or historic-site feature.
Sketch how public recreation and preservation share the site without entering sensitive ground.

packs.title: Central to the Pier
packs.promise: Walk downtown art and the bayfront in one or two afternoons.

q.s: Begin with contemporary art on Central Avenue.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or official-source route.
Choose an accessible work in the free public gallery or its official exhibition page.
Sketch a color or material relationship without copying artist text.

q.s: Read a work with its own label and context.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or official-source route.
Choose one work during an admitted visit or from the museum’s official collection pages.
Record the artist and context from the museum, without generalizing about a living community.

q.t: A Walk Out over the Bay
q.s: Read a public pier as a route, not an event.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or official-source route.
Walk an open public section of the Pier or use its official district map to identify two public zones.
Record how the route changes from land to over-water view and where you would turn back.
